figures.finding: No agreement sets an Irish screen director's pay: the Screen Directors Guild of Ireland is still working to introduce a minimum terms agreement with Screen Producers Ireland, and says directors' pay has been frozen for years.

value.sought: SDGI-SPI minimum terms agreement (film and TV)

sources.said: SDGI’s aim is to create a better working environment for directors through the introduction of minimum terms agreement with Screen Producers Ireland.
productions demand that directors accept pay that has been frozen for years

figures.finding: Irish law (S.I. 567 of 2021) gives a director the right to appropriate and proportionate pay when licensing rights, a yearly account of exploitation, extra pay if the fee proves disproportionately low, and revocation if the work is not exploited.

sources.said: When you license or transfer your exclusive rights to a producer, you are entitled to receive appropriate and proportionate pay and a fair balance of rights and interests.

figures.finding: On Screen Ireland-funded productions contracted from 1 October 2019 an Irish director shares a 60% recoupment corridor: 40% to the production company, 10% to the Irish director and 10% to the Irish writer (documentaries 45/10; series directors split pro rata by episodes).
figures.applies: Ireland, Screen Ireland production funding contracted from 1 October 2019; corridor funds may only be spent on approved development, production, distribution or training.

sources.said: This recoupment corridor shall be broken down as follows: (i) 40% to Production Company, (ii) 10% to Irish Director, and (iii) 10% to Irish Writer.

figures.finding: SDGI membership costs €125 a year and needs two broadcast credits (festival, television or SVOD), one from the last three years.

sources.said: SDGI members must have two broadcast credits i.e. two films/shows screened at a recognised film festival or broadcast on television or SVOD. One of the works must have been made in the last 3 years. Annual membership fees for SDGI are €125.
